facts.rationale: The current body still writes only the two victim arrays and two trailing bytes, while the current HitCapsule layout confirms that all other combat and geometry fields are separate.

evidence.why: Enumerates every current source read and destination write.
Shows the full current HitCapsule layout and the fields outside this selective copy.

facts.value: Implements continuity of hitbox victim history: when fighter or item collision code replaces a hit capsule with another active capsule carrying the same hitbox identifier, previously contacted victims remain recognized instead of being treated as newly encountered solely because a different capsule slot is now in use.
facts.rationale: Current fighter and item callers still select another enabled capsule with the same identifier before copying, and the current collision-library code still maintains and queries the transferred victim histories.

evidence.why: Shows fighter collision code copying history between enabled capsules sharing the same identifier.
Shows item collision code performing the same same-identifier history transfer.
Shows the copied data participating in bounded victim-history bookkeeping.

facts.value: Side-effect-only copy helper with signature `void lbColl_CopyHitCapsule(HitCapsule* src, HitCapsule* dst)`. It copies two parallel arrays of 12 `HitVictim` records and the associated `u8` fields at offsets 0x44 and 0x45.
facts.rationale: The current definition and layout preserve the exact signature, twelve-element array dimensions, HitVictim element type, and byte-sized x44/x45 fields.

evidence.why: Shows the exact current signature, two array copies, and trailing byte assignments.
Defines the current HitVictim arrays as twelve entries and x44/x45 as byte fields.

facts.value: Transfers the complete per-victim collision history from one hit capsule to another so a replacement or duplicate active capsule can continue the source capsule's already-contacted-victim bookkeeping.
facts.rationale: The current target still copies both victim tables and their cursor/count bytes without cloning the rest of the HitCapsule, and current fighter and item callers still use it for same-identifier capsule continuity.

evidence.why: Shows the complete selective victim-history transfer.
Shows the fighter caller copying from another enabled same-identifier capsule or clearing history.
Shows the corresponding item caller and same-identifier selection.

facts.value: Unconditionally makes the destination's two victim-history tables and their replacement cursors identical to the source. This preserves both which victims are currently remembered and where each full twelve-entry table will next overwrite an old entry; it does not alter whether the destination capsule is enabled.
facts.rationale: The current target unconditionally copies the tables and x44/x45, the current layout separates enabled state from those fields, and current neighboring registration routines demonstrate bounded replacement behavior.

evidence.why: Shows the unconditional table and cursor/count copies.
Shows that capsule enabled state is separate from the victim arrays and x44/x45.
Shows neighboring victim registration using the copied bookkeeping for duplicate rejection and bounded replacement.
